subject: POC trial planning: workload & traffic profile intake (AcmeHealth)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC trial planning: workload & traffic profile intake (recap & next steps)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to speak earlier. Wanted to capture the quick recap and next steps so we can lock the POC scope and timeline. Below is what we heard from you and a few items we need to kick off the trial environment.

Quick recap from today's discovery call:
- Goal: validate Redwood inference at AcmeHealth scale for patient-facing summarization workflows and batch reporting.
- Success criteria: ~90% parity on key QA prompts vs current baseline, end-to-end 95th p99 latency < 800ms for interactive flows, and unit cost under agreed target (TBD).
- Timeline: 3-week POC (env + sample workloads + evaluation), preferred start week of Feb 14.
- Stakeholders: Alex (product), Priya (security/compliance), Marissa/Ben (Redwood sales/eng), Dev (Redwood infra contact).

What we need from your side to start provisioning and sizing: (please send by EOD Wed)
1) Workload profile spreadsheet (RPS by endpoint, typical token lengths, concurrency, burst characteristics).
2) A sample of 50-100 representative payloads (redacted PHI if needed) or synthetic equivalents.
3) Success criteria specifics: target QA prompts list and any scoring thresholds.
4) Any network / IP allowlist requirements for Dedicated or Private options.

Attachment: acme_workload_profile.xlsx (template) — fill RPS / token distribution and return.

Proposed next steps:
- You fill the attached sheet -> we size infra and send POC runbook by Feb 11.
- Kickoff call (30m) on Feb 14 to provision and review rollouts.

Thanks — really excited to get started.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC trial planning: workload & traffic profile intake (recap & next steps)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the template. Quick answers inline below and I've attached a populated copy of the sheet.

- RPS / traffic:
  - Interactive summarization endpoint: typical steady-state ~15 RPS, peak bursts up to 120 RPS for short periods (2-5 min) during morning syncs.
  - Batch reporting job (nightly): ~500 requests total over a 2-hour window (large tokens).
- Token lengths: interactive median ~220 tokens input, expected completion ~180 tokens; batch jobs can hit 8k token inputs (we truncate/stream as needed).
- Concurrency: production front-end runs ~40 concurrent interactive sessions typically, but backends can queue.
- Burst pattern: irregular peaks associated with sync jobs / ED shift changes; most bursts are <10 minutes.

I've attached acme_workload_profile.xlsx (populated) and a ZIP of 30 sample payloads (redacted). Let me know if the payloads need further anonymization.

Priya: we'll need to loop security for the POC environment — are there any specific logs/retention requirements we should note now?

Happy to jump on the Feb 14 kickoff — 10:30am PT works for us.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Product Manager, Clinical Systems
AcmeHealth
alex.johnson@acmehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2027 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC trial planning: workload & traffic profile intake (recap & next steps)

Thanks Alex — that's super helpful. Couple operational notes and a proposed POC run cadence:

Operational notes:
- We'll stand up a scoped POC cluster with autoscaling and a staging dataset. Dev will be the primary infra contact for provisioning IP allowlists and initial perf runs.
- For the large-token batch jobs (8k inputs), we'll run a few pilot batches to validate memory/KV behavior and measure cost.

Proposed 3-week POC plan (high level):
Week 0 (prep, Feb 14): kickoff, upload sample payloads, finalize success criteria doc.
Week 1 (perf runs): run interactive perf tests (rps sweep, concurrency, burst sims), iterate on kernel/quantization profiles.
Week 2 (scale & validation): run batch jobs and end-to-end QA scoring against your baseline.
Week 3 (analysis & handoff): compile report, cost estimates, recommended config for production.

Action items for AcmeHealth:
- Confirm kickoff time (Marissa suggested Feb 14 10:30am PT).
- Share the 50-100 sample payloads (Alex attached ~30 - please add another 20-70 if possible).
- Sign off on success criteria doc (we'll draft based on the prompts you provide).

Dev (cc): could you reserve instance pool for a 3-week window starting Feb 14 and confirm preferred GPU type (we recommend A10G for interactive + A100S for large-batch memory) - flag any constraints.

Alex - we'll also need a contact on your side for quick triage during perf runs (Slack/PagerDuty) so we can iterate quickly.

Thanks - Ben

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the populated sheet and the sample payloads - that's perfect to start. Confirming the kickoff at Feb 14, 10:30am PT. Below is the evaluation plan and owners (please review and reply with any changes by Fri Feb 12):

Evaluation plan & success criteria (draft):
- Functional: 90%+ pass rate on 10 key clinical QA prompts (Acme to provide prompt set and scoring rubric). Owner: AcmeHealth (Priya/Product).
- Latency: 95th/99th for interactive endpoint <= 800ms end-to-end under target 15 RPS steady with simulated bursts to 120 RPS. Owner: Redwood (Ben/Dev).
- Cost: Estimated unit cost <= $0.02 per interactive completion (TBD after initial runs). Owner: Redwood pricing/Marissa.
- Stability: No loss of KV cache across 25-minute sessions and successful handling of batch jobs without OOMs. Owner: Redwood (Dev).

Data & security checkpoints:
- We will use redacted sample payloads and a dedicated staging environment. Priya, please list any additional evidence or controls (SOC2 artifacts, logging) you need for evaluation. Owner: AcmeHealth security / Redwood security team.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Feb 11: Redwood sends POC runbook (based on your sheet) - Ben/Dev.
- Feb 14: Kickoff + provisioning (30m) - all.
- Feb 14-21: Perf runs & iterative tuning - Redwood lead: Dev, Acme lead: Alex.
- Feb 22-25: Batch validation & QA scoring - joint.
- Feb 26: Final report + recommendations - Redwood (Marissa/Ben).

Please reply to confirm owners and the timeline. If all good we'll share the POC runbook by Feb 11 and provisioning checklist.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
